results.title: Netherlands 2026 World Cup Preview - Squad, Schedule, Odds & Tips
highlights:
The Netherlands head to the 2026 World Cup as Group F favorites, boasting a robust defense led by Virgil van Dijk and a talented squad managed by Ronald Koeman. Oranje topped qualifying with ease and feature stars such as Frenkie de Jong and Memphis Depay, though the latter’s fitness is in question. Bookmakers give the Dutch 21/1 odds to lift the trophy—eighth best—while group odds heavily favor them over Japan, Sweden, and Tunisia. Expect Netherlands to top their group, but their likely knockout route could mean a tough test against Brazil or Morocco.

## Group F Schedule and Path to the Final
[...]
The Netherlands have been drawn in Group F where they begin against Japan in Arlington. They face Sweden in Houston before ending against Tunisia in Kansas City where the team is based.
[...]
Topping the group will see Ronald Koeman's side face the Group C runners-up - likely to be Brazil or Morocco. They would then have a winnable match in the Round of 16 before facing a group winner in the quarter-finals, possibly Germany or France.
[...]
Finishing second in the group would set up a Round of 32 match against the winners of Group C, once again Brazil or Morocco. That path would be likely to result in a quarter-final against England or Croatia.

results.title: Netherlands at the World Cup 2026: Can Oranje Finally Deliver? · Cup26 AI
highlights:
Netherlands at the World Cup 2026: Can Oranje Finally Deliver? · Cup26 AI
[...]
Team preview · 2026 FIFA World Cup
[...]
The Netherlands arrive at the 2026 World Cup carrying the familiar burden of being good enough to dream but never quite good enough to finish the job. Ronald Koeman's side qualified in style, topping UEFA Group G unbeaten with 20 points from eight matches, six wins and only two draws, both against Poland. They scored 27 and conceded just four, sealing a 12th World Cup appearance with a 4-0 win over Lithuania. On paper the Oranje are a serious, well-drilled team. The question, as ever, is whether the talent converts into a deep run.
[...]
The spine is genuinely elite. Captain Virgil van Dijk anchors the defence, Frenkie de Jong dictates from midfield, and a Liverpool-heavy attacking core of Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch sits alongside Manchester City's Tijjani Reijnders. Up front, all-time leading scorer Memphis Depay— now on 55 international goals after overtaking Robin van Persie — recovered from a thigh injury just in time to make Koeman's final 26-man squad. The depth is thinner than it looks, though: Xavi Simons (ruptured ACL), Matthijs de Ligt and Stefan de Vrij are all out injured, and Jeremie Frimpong was a notable omission.
[...]
The draw was relatively kind. The Netherlands sit in Group F alongside Japan, Sweden and Tunisia. They open against Japan on June 14 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, face Sweden on June 20 at NRG Stadium in Houston, and close against Tunisia on June 25 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City. Japan are the most dangerous of the three and Sweden carry a physical threat, but with the top two plus the best third-placed teams advancing in this 48-team format, the Oranje should reach the Round of 32 comfortably barring a collapse.
[...]
The realistic ceiling is the trickier conversation. This Netherlands group has the individual quality to beat anyone on a good night, and a kind early bracket could carry them to the quarter-finals or further. But the defensive injuries, an aging Depay leading the line, and Koeman's tendency toward caution all cap the upside. A semi-final would be a strong tournament; the final, while not absurd, would require the kind of momentum and luck the Dutch have rarely strung together at a World Cup.
[...]
That is why our prediction model rates the Netherlands as long shots for the title — clear of the second tier of contenders but well behind favourites Spain, Argentina and France. Whether you back the Oranje to outperform that billing or expect another familiar disappointment, you can test every possible knockout path yourself in our interactive simulator.

Belgium vs Iran is shaping up to be one of the most tactically lopsided yet strategically consequential fixtures of Group G at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. This is Matchday 2 for both sides, meaning both teams will already know their opening results before a ball is kicked at SoFi Stadium. For Belgium, ranked 9th in the world and widely considered Group G favourites, a win here would almost certainly guarantee progression to the Round of 32. For IR Iran — ranked 20th and making their fourth straight World Cup appearance — a point or shock victory could transform their entire tournament.
[...]
The match is played on neutral soil in Los Angeles, removing any home advantage, but Belgium’s superior squad depth, European pedigree, and top-10 FIFA ranking make them heavy favourites for the Belgium vs Iran prediction. That said, Iran are not to be underestimated: they qualified impressively through the AFC, conceding fewer than one goal per match across 16 qualifying games.

Belgium are heavy favourites in virtually every Belgium vs Iran prediction model, backed by their FIFA ranking (9th vs 20th), superior club-level competition, and deeper squad. Iran’s low ceiling in recent friendlies against modest opposition further inflates Belgium’s probability, though an upset is always possible at a World Cup.
[...]
Belgium 2–0 IR Iran
[...]
Belgium are expected to control large portions of the game, create multiple clear-cut chances, and ultimately find goals through their wide attackers or a set-piece situation. Iran’s disciplined defence may frustrate Belgium in the first half, but the quality differential should tell in the second. A clean sheet for Belgium reflects Iran’s counter-threat being largely neutralised through Belgium’s possession-heavy approach. A 2–1 result (Iran scoring a late consolation) is the second most likely scenario if Iran manage a set-piece or rapid transition goal.
[...]
Most analysts predict a Belgium win in the Belgium vs Iran World Cup 2026 match. Belgium are ranked 9th in the world versus Iran’s 20th, carry superior squad quality with players at top European clubs, and had an outstanding qualifying campaign scoring 29 goals in 8 matches. Our predicted score is Belgium 2–0 IR Iran, though a 2–1 margin remains a realistic alternative if Iran find a late consolation.
